data.description:
Closes the cross-contamination gap from sc-2. Ensures that .claude/scripts/dso ticket list --has-tag=detected_by:tests returns only bug-type tickets filed at or after M1 ship date. The implementation may take the form of (a) a tag-namespace policy enforced at tag-apply time that rejects detected_by:* on non-bug tickets, (b) a query-side filter that intersects the has-tag result with --type=bug, or (c) both. The story selects the approach during implementation but must satisfy the observable outcome.

## Done Definitions

- A non-bug ticket that carries a detected_by:<channel> tag does not appear in the result of .claude/scripts/dso ticket list --has-tag=detected_by:tests ← Satisfies: sc-2
- A bug ticket filed at or after M1 ship date that carries detected_by:tests does appear in the result ← Satisfies: sc-2
- Test exercises both cases (non-bug with tag is excluded; bug with tag is included) ← Satisfies: sc-2
- At ship time, a scan for existing non-bug tickets with detected_by:* tags is performed and any found are listed for remediation (either tag-remove or accepted as known exceptions with written rationale) ← Satisfies: sc-2

## Considerations

- [Reliability] If the chosen approach is a query-side filter, ensure every documented query path in calibration-report.sh and /dso:test-quality-report uses the filter — otherwise a future query path could regress sc-2.
- [Performance] If the chosen approach is enforcement at tag-apply time, ensure the check does not add measurable latency to every tag command (only detected_by:* needs the check).

## Escalation Policy

Escalate when blocked
data.title: As a calibration-program operator, I want detected_by tags to be queryable only on bug-type tickets, so that channel queries are not contaminated by non-bug tickets that accidentally carry the tag.
